bullets.title: NVDA: Beat/raise on earnings but stock -13% WTD amid CEO crisis, SEC probe, China chip halt
bullets.body: NVDA posted Q3 revenue of $115.8B (+103% YoY, beat by ~6%), guided Q4 to $130B ±3%, and raised FY28 growth to ~75% from 70%. Vera Rubin contributed ~$20B in its first quarter. Despite this, the stock fell sharply on week: Jensen Huang ousting fallout, board ruling out his reinstatement, SEC civil probe into potential accounting issues, halt of Hopper/H200 shipments to China (~$2.4B quarterly revenue), and new BIS export controls restricting remote access to AI chips in SE Asia/Brazil. Total supply commitments rose to ~$430B; $227B buyback authorized through FY27. Jefferies cut PT to $250; UBS cut PT to $220 (from $300); Piper to $230; GS maintains Buy at $220. Semis sector (SOX) -17% on the week.

bullets.title: NVDA export controls: BIS restricts SE Asia chip access, TSMC/Samsung halt China shipments
bullets.body: The Commerce Department issued an interim final rule requiring licenses for advanced AI chip exports to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil to prevent circumvention via offshore data centers. TSMC and Samsung halted shipments of advanced chips (16nm and below) to Chinese customers pending US license reviews. NVDA's server partners also suspended SE Asia shipments. These rules rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule and are estimated to strip 1-2 GW from AI chip demand near-term.

bullets.title: INTU: FQ1 beat but Credit Karma guidance slashed 60%; Mailchimp sold; stock -10%
bullets.body: INTU reported FQ1 revenue of $4.35B (+12% YoY, beat). However, Credit Karma FY27 guidance was cut to 3-7% from 11-13%, with management citing higher rates and faster-than-expected shift to AI-powered consumer discovery. FY27 consolidated revenue guidance lowered to 8-9% from 9-10%. Mailchimp being sold to Bending Spoons for $3.68B with INTU reinvesting $368M back. Stock -9-10% on the news. UBS cuts PT to $315 (Neutral); Mizuho to $380 (OW); KeyBanc to $375 (OW).

bullets.title: BILL: TPG/Corpay take-private at $63.25/sh; multiple downgrades across Street
bullets.body: BILL agreed to be acquired by TPG (majority) and Corpay (minority, ~$1.1B for ~1/3 stake with 2030 option to acquire remainder) at $63.25/share in an all-cash deal, valuing the company at ~$6.0B (~4.2x EV/NTM revenue). Deal represents 31% premium to 60-day VWAP; expected to close 1H27. Mizuho, JPMorgan, UBS, KeyBanc, Jefferies, TD Cowen all downgraded to Neutral/equivalent with PTs matching deal price.

bullets.title: ORCL: Secured all OpenAI funding; targets $30B+ FCF in FY29, $225B revenue by FY30
bullets.body: Oracle confirmed it has secured all funding needed to fulfill its OpenAI contract with a $10B equity and $10B debt raise complete. The Abilene Astra-6 campus is nearly complete; Shackelford gigawatt-scale campus fully permitted. NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack handover on track. FY27 revenue guidance >$90B (+34% YoY cc); targeting >$225B in FY30 (35%+ CAGR). Positive FCF expected H2 FY28, targeting >$30B FCF in FY29.

bullets.title: DIS: F4Q26 beat with double-digit FY27 guidance; dividend raised 33%, $9B buyback planned
bullets.body: Disney reported F4Q26 EPS of $1.77 (beat consensus $1.67) and revenue of $25.95B (beat $25.16B). Management guided FY27 adjusted EPS to double-digit growth, raised annual dividend 33% to $2.00/share, and guided $9B in share repurchases and $11B FCF. Parks domestic attendance +11% (3% ex-53rd week); SVOD OI margins 13.6%. Analysts broadly lifted PTs: GS to $143, Wells Fargo to $140, UBS to $133 (Buy). DIS also planning $3B annual opex savings by FY29 to fund content and growth.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI launches with $3.79B Day-1 sales, 99 Metacritic, 32.5M presold units
bullets.body: Rockstar Games announced GTA VI day-one retail sales of $3.79B, well ahead of UBS's $3.6B full-FQ27 forecast. Take-Two announced 32.5M presold units; Sensor Tower tracked ~24.6M total units. The game achieved a 99 Metacritic score (tied all-time high) and peaked at 3.31M concurrent Twitch viewers (5.5x the prior record). UBS and other analysts raised unit estimates materially; each 10M unit upside = ~$600M bookings vs. the $8.0-8.2B guide.

bullets.title: DLR/data center REITs: -8-9% WTD on AI regulation, BIS restrictions, Trump overseas DC tax threat
bullets.body: Data center REITs fell ~8.75% for the week, with DLR specifically -9.73%. Headwinds included: Trump vowing to tax US companies building data centers abroad, BIS remote access restrictions threatening APAC data center buildout (DLR may need to be more selective with customer bookings), Loudoun County VA adopting a 12-month data center pause, and North Carolina governor calling for tax incentive repeals. Citi upgraded EQIX and DLR to Buy and maintains BXDC Buy ($20.50 PT) on the $5B AWS sale-leaseback at 7% cap rate.

bullets.title: GOOGL: JPM reiterates OW at $375 PT; Gemini 4 Neon launches, Tasks agent rollout, YouTube $3B settlement
bullets.body: JPM reiterates Overweight on GOOGL with $375 Dec-27 PT (22x 2028E GAAP EPS of $17). Three new Gemini 4 models released in <1 month; Hydrogen now powers Search globally; Neon ranks #3 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 32% lower cost per task than Carbon. Gemini Tasks launched as free agent to 1B+ users. Cloud revenue grew +103% YoY in Q3 with $561B backlog. Separately, YouTube finalizing ~$3B settlement with schools over social media addiction claims. Waymo temporarily banned from California freeways. AVGO: Google cutting 2027 Broadcom TPU shipments ~20% (~1M units), shifting some to MediaTek.

bullets.title: AMD: -7-8% WTD on Hunterbrook short report alleging China server exposure; AMD denies claims
bullets.body: AMD fell sharply after Hunterbrook Capital published a short report alleging AMD has problematic China server exposure via firmware access to Chinese server maker IEIT Systems. AMD disputed the allegations citing legal compliance. Separately, congressional reports showed Commerce approved ~879K NVDA and AMD AI chips for China (26% of 3.4M requested), including to some military-linked entities. AMD also completed the $8.2B all-stock acquisition of World Labs (AI/spatial intelligence, Fei-Fei Li joins as EVP).

bullets.title: MSFT: Ignite bullish on Azure/M365 AI adoption; RBC reiterates OW at $640 PT; undetected July bug caused major outage
bullets.body: MSFT Ignite reinforced the full-stack AI thesis with strong M365 Copilot/Cowork demand, E7 adoption, and Fabric/agent deployment. RBC reiterates Outperform at $640 PT. ByteDance reportedly in advanced talks to spend $500M on Azure for OpenAI models. However, a software bug undetected since July triggered a cascading Outlook/Teams global outage affecting ~500M people for 15 hours. Citi reiterates Buy at $680 PT citing accelerating M365 monetization.

bullets.title: CRDO/MRVL: CRDO settles patent dispute with MRVL; LITE/MRVL merger faces China approval headwinds
bullets.body: Credo Technology settled its patent dispute with Marvell Technology over data-center cable technology; terms were confidential. The settlement was viewed positively for CRDO. Separately, the LITE/MRVL merger faces concerns over China regulatory approval given US restrictions on Chinese optical transceivers, with Morgan Stanley noting the ban would eliminate demand channels for LITE's China-manufactured products.

bullets.title: CCL/RCL: Cruise channel checks bullish; CCL orders new ships, Celebration Key still driving demand
bullets.body: UBS cruise channel check shows overall booking volumes at mid-single-digit YoY growth. CCL Princess outperforming on strong marketing; Celebration Key still driving demand; Princess now also calling at the island; water park delayed to 2030. Caribbean pricing +5%, Europe +6%, Alaska +7% YoY. Norwegian lagging with flat-to-+1% pricing vs. peers +3-7%. CCL ordering two new ships (3,690 berths each) for 2033 and 2035. Morgan Stanley raised CCL PT to $32.50.

bullets.title: SPOT: CFO at TMT conf signals mid-teens revenue CAGR through 2030; AI Remix tool close to launch
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on SPOT at $700 PT (~30x FY28e FCF). CFO guided mid-teens total revenue growth through 2030 from subscriber growth, pricing, and ad acceleration. Gross margin target 35-40% by 2030. Advertising revenue accelerated to +9% cc in Q3. AI Remix tool licensing agreements signed with UMG, Believe, Kobalt; Q1 2027 launch pending artist opt-ins. LYV partnership 'Reserve by Spotify' expanding to Europe and Australia in 2027.

bullets.title: BE: Upgraded to OW at BMO, MS raises PT to $335 on third guidance raise; 100+ prospective customers
bullets.body: Bloom Energy received an upgrade to Outperform at BMO Capital Markets. Morgan Stanley raised its PT to $335 (Overweight), citing a third guidance raise for the year, expanding demand from utilities/international/C&I customers, positive carbon capture commercialization signs, and continued margin expansion. BE's customer event drew 100+ prospective customers; a 370MW Texas deployment (Lone Oak project) filed with FERC. NTT 900MW deal cited.

bullets.title: MDB: UBS upgrades to Buy at $450 PT; acquires Firebolt; CEO departure creates near-term overhang
bullets.body: UBS upgraded MongoDB from Neutral to Buy, raising PT to $450 (from $375), citing durable 20%+ revenue growth and 25%+ Atlas growth. MDB also acquired Firebolt for real-time analytics capabilities (terms undisclosed). However, Hedgeye moved MDB to Short Bench following CEO CJ Desai's departure for Meta, plus exits of Chief Customer Officer and AI head; analysts note potential stalling of large enterprise deals without permanent CEO.

bullets.title: WSM: Q3 comp miss on Pottery Barn; Citi cuts PT to $245, stock -15% on elevated expectations
bullets.body: Williams-Sonoma reported Q3 EPS of $2.38 (beat consensus $2.19) but comps of +5.1% missed the ~5.6% estimate, primarily due to Pottery Barn deceleration to +1.8% (vs. +5.1% prior quarter). FY26 guidance was reiterated. Supply chain challenges including port congestion, inventory delays extending into FY27, and elevated fuel/freight costs flagged. Citi cut PT to $245 (from $275, Neutral). Stock fell ~15% as it had been trading near peak valuations.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE: Upcoming earnings catalysts; DELL AI server momentum strong into F3Q27
bullets.body: DELL reports Tuesday 11/24 after close with consensus expecting $49.3B revenue (+150% ISG) and $6.62 EPS; AI-Optimized Servers $19.83B in Q3 with FY AI Server revenue ~$74B (3x YoY). Options imply ~14.6% move. HPE reports Monday 11/23 after close with consensus at $14.47B revenue, $1.28 EPS; bulls cite AI PC and server pricing, networking strength. JPM favors DELL and HPE into earnings over NTAP and HPQ on AI infrastructure fundamentals.

bullets.title: HOOD: Added to Wolfe Alpha List at 23x 2028 EPS; Mizuho bullish on wealth-creation platform
bullets.body: Wolfe Research added Robinhood to its Alpha List, citing a ~36% QTD decline to 23x 2028 EPS (low end of historic 20-60x range) with strong fundamental trading pipeline and competitive/regulatory risks viewed as overblown. Mizuho rates HOOD Outperform at $130 PT, highlighting $35B+ in retirement assets, 1.3M Gold Card holders, agentic trading with 200K accounts, and prediction markets diversifying to 30% non-sports. Kalshi's equities entry not viewed as a strategic threat.

bullets.title: BABA: Q2 cloud revenue +67% YoY above 50% expectations; combined AI losses narrowing to near-zero
bullets.body: Alibaba reported Q2 cloud external recurring revenue growing 67% YoY, well above ~50% investor expectations. Cloud EBITA margin expanded to 14.5% (from ~12% prior quarter). AI Labs losses narrowed: combined cloud EBITA covered 84% of AI Labs losses, with combined loss falling to RMB1.7B from RMB8.2B QoQ. T-Head Zhenwu V900 chip mass production begins Q1 2027. FY30 target of $100B external cloud revenue with >20% margin maintained. JPM maintains OW at $200 PT.
